notes:
Summary: Enterprise evaluation focused on Dedicated capacity economics (reserved GPU commit) and SLA guarantees. Aurora Lattice runs high-volume recommendation reranking + embeddings for personalization. Primary ask: predictable unit cost per token under reserved commitment, latency SLOs for interactive paths, and clear burst policy for marketing spikes.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2026-01-28: Intro call (AE Maya Chen) — Aurora overview, initial interest in Dedicated for production personalization.
- 2026-02-09: Technical deep-dive (SE Lucas) — shared expected QPS and token distributions; recorded (ff_2026-02-09).
- 2026-02-24: Security questionnaire submitted; requested KMS details and residency options.
- 2026-03-04: Dedicated demo + capacity planning session; ran two sizing scenarios (8-GPU vs 16-GPU); transcript: ff_2026-03-04_dedicated-demo.
- 2026-03-10: Pricing workshop — introduced committed tiers and burst rates.

Workload profile (Aurora provided):
- Peak concurrent queries: 120 QPS for short chat/recommends, average request size 80 tokens (input+output).
- Background bulk jobs: embedding index updates ~200M tokens/month (batch tolerant).
- Traffic pattern: predictable daily peaks 10:00–12:00 & 18:00–20:00 PST; marketing campaigns cause infrequent 3x bursts.

Latency and throughput SLO targets discussed:
- Interactive reranking path: p95 < 90ms, p99 < 280ms (10k-context routing disabled).
- Embedding generation batch: throughput goal 40k tokens/sec aggregate across cluster during rebuild windows.
- Availability target: 99.95% monthly for Dedicated pools; need 4 hr maintenance window notice.

Reserved capacity options evaluated (high-level):
- Option A (8 GPUs, committed):
  - Estimated monthly list cost: ~$120,000/month (incl infra & support).
  - Planning assumption: average utilization 45% (baseline traffic + predictable peaks).
  - Effective cost per 1M generated tokens (compute-only): ~$2.1 (assumes amortized hw + infra + ops).
  - Notes: can support ~80 QPS at target latency for reranking path; batch jobs scheduled overnight.
- Option B (16 GPUs, committed + burst pool):
  - Estimated monthly list cost: ~$220,000/month (lower unit cost due to scale).
  - Planning assumption: average utilization 60% (Aurora expects growth + marketing bursts).
  - Effective cost per 1M generated tokens: ~$1.3.
  - Burst policy: additional pay-as-you-go capacity available at premium during >baseline 2x peaks.
- Option C (8 GPUs committed + private burst/day):
  - Monthly commitment: ~$110,000 + burst spend (~$20k typical during campaigns).
  - Estimated blended unit cost per 1M tokens: ~$1.9 (if burst used twice/month).

Unit economics & assumptions (from Redwood TCO workbook v2):
- GPU unit amortization + licensing + rack infra + networking + ops allocated to customer: ~60–70% of committed spend.
- Idle capacity buffer: planning assumes 10% headroom for scheduling latency-sensitive requests.
- Token accounting: billable tokens = input + output; embedding vectorization overhead accounted separately.
- Example calc (Option B): $220k/mo -> $2.64M/yr. At 60% util -> effective consumed compute = $1.584M/yr. If Aurora projects 1.2B tokens/yr of generated output on the committed pool -> compute-only cost ~$1.32 per 1M tokens. With monitoring, storage, and support add ~0.02–0.1 per 1M tokens -> blended ~$1.3–1.4 per 1M.

SLA and negotiation points flagged:
- SLA credit mechanism: Aurora wants credits to be automatically applied for p99 > 350ms across >30 minutes (they prefer hard credits not ticket-driven). Need legal to review.
- Maintenance/eviction: clarify automatic fallback to hosted API or other region for critical endpoints during unplanned infra failures.
- Data residency: require logs & audit trail retention for 2 years in-region (NA-East).

Risk & open technical questions:
- Quantifying actual effective utilization post-launch — initial spikes could drive underutilization outside campaign windows, affecting unit economics.
- Cold-cache token cost: heavy prefix reuse in personalization could improve effective token cost; need to pilot caching strategies.
- GPU family choice: H100-class preferable for long-context models; cost delta vs A100 needs confirmation for final pricing.

Next steps agreed with customer:
- Redwood to deliver a final TCO workbook with 3-year amortization, sensitivity to utilization (30%/45%/60%), and per-token unit economics for each commit tier by 2026-03-19.
- Legal to draft SLA redline responding to Aurora's auto-credit request by 2026-03-26.
- Schedule 2-week POC (trial dedicated pool with synthetic traffic) after signoff — target start 2026-05-01.

Stenographic notes (shorthand quotes):
- "We absolutely need predictable per-token economics for Q3 campaigns" — Head of ML Ops.
- "If the burst policy is clear and credits are automatic, we can commit 16 GPUs" — CTO (paraphrase).

Attachments / artifacts: pricing workbook (drive://redwood/pricing/aurora-tco-v2.xlsx), security questionnaire + answers (drive://redwood/security/aurora-security-faq.pdf), demo recording ff_2026-03-04_dedicated-demo.

Sales call guidance for AE/SEs:
- Emphasize Optimize recommendations (quant profiles, batching & caching) to reduce effective unit cost by up to 20% without changing commit level.
- Offer a 60-day pilot on a reduced-price committed tier to validate utilization curves; capture real token telemetry for final ARR sizing.
- Prepare legal brief on automatic credits and latency measurement methodology (sampling window and synthetic probe placement).
